headline: SECP Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines Issued
annotation: SECP set up a regulatory sandbox, initially cohort based. The January 2019 date is carried over from the first version and was not re-checked. Fintechs working on tokenized securities, robo-advisory, or crowdfunding could test products without full licensing. The sandbox accepted proposals in quarterly cycles, providing a supervised path to market for capital-market innovations.
sourcePublisher: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
sourceTitle: Regulatory sandbox page
label: Primary, not re-checked

headline: National Payment Systems Strategy (NPSS) Published
annotation: The NPSS laid out the entire roadmap for Raast and digital payment infrastructure. For builders, this is the foundational document that defines how instant payments, open banking APIs, and interoperability standards will evolve. Any fintech designing payment flows in Pakistan should treat this as the architectural blueprint.
sourceTitle: National Payment Systems Strategy page
label: Primary, not re-checked

headline: Raast Bulk Payments Module Launched
annotation: The first phase of Pakistan's instant payment system went live with bulk disbursements: government salaries, pensions, and social grants. For builders, this established the core clearing infrastructure that P2P and P2M modules would later plug into. Integration required connecting through SBP's participant framework.
sourceTitle: Press release on the launch of the first phase of Raast
label: Primary

headline: Digital Bank Licensing Framework Issued
annotation: SBP created two licence types: Digital Retail Bank (DRB) and Digital Full Bank (DFB), with minimum capital of PKR 1.5B for DRBs scaling to PKR 4B over three years. This means a fintech can now obtain a full banking license without physical branches. The framework requires robust digital governance and data management: any aspiring neobank needs to design for these from day one. Capital figures are from the March 2026 reading and were not re-checked.
sourceTitle: Licensing and regulatory framework for digital banks (BPRD 2022 Circular 1 annex)
label: Primary, not re-checked

headline: Raast P2P Instant Transfers Go Live
annotation: Consumers could now send money instantly and free of charge using just a mobile number (RAAST ID) through their bank's app. For builders, this opened the door to embedding instant transfers into any product: wallets, lending apps, or marketplaces: via Raast's API layer. KYC-verified bank accounts are the minimum requirement for senders and receivers.
sourceTitle: Raast P2P page
label: Primary, not re-checked

headline: Revised EMI Regulations 2023 Issued
annotation: The revised framework dramatically expanded what EMIs can do: payment aggregation, bill aggregation, escrow services for e-commerce, API services to other fintechs, and inward cross-border remittances. Wallet limits were increased, and minors and freelancers became eligible customers. If you are building a wallet or payment product, these regulations define your ceiling.
sourceTitle: Regulations for Electronic Money Institutions 2023 (PSD 2023 Circular 3 enclosure)
label: Primary, not re-checked

headline: Personal Data Protection Bill 2023 Approved by Cabinet
annotation: Pakistan's first comprehensive data privacy legislation was approved by the Federal Cabinet and sent to Parliament. It establishes a National Commission for Personal Data Protection and requires explicit consent frameworks, breach notification, and cross-border data transfer controls. Any fintech handling PII needs to architect consent management and data audit trails now, even before final enactment. Status update: the World Bank's 2026 regional assessment still lists Pakistan's data protection law as a draft, so the bill is not binding law.
sourceTitle: Final draft Personal Data Protection Bill, May 2023
label: Primary, not re-checked

extraSources.title: Digital Public Infrastructure for Inclusive Growth: A Regional Assessment for the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan, p. 46 (local copy of the PDF)
extraSources.label: Primary

headline: Regulatory Sandbox Restructured to Always-Open
annotation: SECP moved from cohort-based intake to year-round applications across three streams: Islamic finance, conventional finance, and women-focused initiatives. This removes the timing constraint for startups: you can apply whenever your product is ready rather than waiting for the next cohort window.
sourcePublisher: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
sourceTitle: Regulatory sandbox page
label: Primary, not re-checked

headline: Five Digital Bank In-Principle Approvals Granted
annotation: Easypaisa, Mashreq Bank, Raqami Islamic Digital Bank, HugoBank, and KT Bank received In-Principle Approval to prepare for operational readiness. This validated that SBP's digital bank framework was moving from policy to execution. For the ecosystem, it signaled that branchless banking at scale was imminent and third-party service providers should prepare integration capabilities.
sourceTitle: Digital bank regulatory page
label: Primary, not re-checked

headline: Raast P2M Service Launched
annotation: Merchant payments on Pakistan's instant payment rail became operational, with all regulated entities required to enable P2M capabilities by March 2024. The system uses SBP's indigenous QR code standard. For builders, this means any merchant-facing product can now accept instant payments via a standardized QR flow rather than proprietary integrations.
sourceTitle: PSD 2023 Circular 4
label: Primary, not re-checked

headline: First Digital Retail Bank License Granted
annotation: Easypaisa Bank Limited became Pakistan's first licensed digital retail bank, authorized for full commercial operations. This is the proof point that the 2022 framework actually delivers licenses. Competing fintechs now face a licensed digital-first competitor with Telenor's distribution reach. Mashreq Bank received pilot approval shortly after in February.
sourceTitle: Press release, 28 January 2025
label: Primary, not re-checked

headline: Raast Participation Criteria Published
annotation: SBP opened Raast access beyond banks to fintechs, payment aggregators, and even educational institutions through four participant categories: direct settlement, direct non-settlement, payment initiation service providers, and indirect participants. This is the open banking enabler: non-bank fintechs can now initiate payments on Raast directly rather than routing through a banking partner.
sourceTitle: PSP&OD Circular No. 01 of 2025: Raast Participation Criteria
label: Primary

headline: SBP Regulatory Sandbox Launched
annotation: SBP launched its own sandbox under Vision 2028, separate from SECP's. The first cohort themes: open banking, inward remittances, and remote merchant onboarding: reveal SBP's priorities. Participants get six months of supervised live testing. If you are building an open banking product, this is the lowest-risk path to regulatory approval.
sourceTitle: SBP launches regulatory sandbox to foster innovation in fintech sector
label: Secondary, not re-checked

headline: Consolidated Customer Onboarding Framework (BPRD 01/2025)
annotation: SBP brought customer onboarding rules into one framework in which biometric verification is the primary method, with NADRA Verisys as a fallback only where biometrics are not possible. For builders, account opening and wallet activation flows need NADRA biometric checks. The circular number, date and compliance deadline in the first version (BPRD 01/2025, 25 July 2025, October 2025) were not visible in the document I read and are unconfirmed.
sourceTitle: Consolidated Customer Onboarding Framework
label: Primary (circular number, date and deadline not shown in the document)

headline: Digital Rupee CBDC Pilot Planned; Soramitsu Reported as Partner
annotation: SBP's governor said the bank was preparing a CBDC pilot, and Dawn, citing Nikkei Asia, reported that Japan's Soramitsu would work with SBP on it. In January 2026 the pilot was still described as planned, and SBP's FY26 payment systems review does not mention it. Live status unconfirmed as of 17 November 2026. For builders, a CBDC would be a new rail alongside Raast if it goes ahead.
sourceTitle: Pakistan picks Japanese company for digital currency rollout
label: Secondary (reports a Nikkei Asia story)

headline: PRISM+ Goes Live on ISO 20022
annotation: SBP launched PRISM+, the upgraded large value settlement system, moving the RTGS to the ISO 20022 messaging standard across retail and large value payments. For builders, ISO 20022 brings richer, structured payment data that reconciliation and compliance tools can use.
sourceTitle: Annual Payment Systems Review FY 2025-26, pp. 8 and 13
label: Primary

headline: 1LINK Designated as a Payment System
annotation: SBP notified 1LINK, which runs shared ATM switching, interbank transfers, bill payments and PayPak, as a Designated Payment System under the Payment Systems and Electronic Fund Transfers Act 2007. This brings closer oversight and alignment with international standards for infrastructure that many fintech flows depend on.
sourceTitle: Annual Payment Systems Review FY 2025-26, p. 22
label: Primary

headline: Technology Risk Management Framework for Payment Institutions
annotation: PSP&OD Circular No. 04 of 2025 set baseline technology and cyber risk requirements for PSOs, PSPs and EMIs, covering security, fraud controls, third party and cloud risk, continuity and incident reporting, with compliance due by 31 March 2026. Any payment fintech needs these controls in place.
sourceTitle: PSP&OD Circular No. 04 of 2025 (described in the Annual Payment Systems Review FY 2025-26, pp. 22 to 23)
accessed: 17 November 2026 (via the FY26 review; circular page not opened)
label: Primary

headline: Digital Identity & NDEL Regulations 2025 Issued
annotation: NADRA issued the Digital Identity Regulations 2025, which let citizens verify identity online without physical documents, and the National Data Exchange Layer (NDEL) Regulations 2025, a standard framework for data sharing between government agencies and authorised private organisations. For fintechs, this points toward digital ID checks and structured data exchange in onboarding. The first version said digital credentials were made legally equivalent to the CNIC; the report I read does not say that.
sourceTitle: NADRA issues landmark digital ID and data exchange regulations
label: Secondary

headline: Critical Telecom Infrastructure Security Regulations 2025
annotation: PTA mandated data localization for all telecom operators, required CISO appointments, annual cyber audits, and 24-hour incident reporting under a Zero Trust security model aligned with ISO 27001 and NIST CSF. Fintechs dependent on telecom infrastructure for mobile money or USSD channels need to understand that their underlying carriers now face strict compliance obligations that could affect uptime SLAs and data handling agreements.
sourceTitle: Critical Telecom Data and Infrastructure Security Regulations 2025
accessed: Tried 17 November 2026; site blocks automated readers
label: Primary, not re-checked

headline: First Regulatory Sandbox Cohort Shortlisted
annotation: Six applicants were shortlisted: three for open banking (Neem, Digi Khata, Swich Retail), one for remote merchant onboarding (The Bank of Punjab), and two for inward remittances (Barq Fintech, and Taptap Send UK with United Bank Limited). Testing runs for up to six months. Builders in adjacent spaces should study these participants, because they show where SBP wants evidence before writing rules.
sourceTitle: SBP announces the shortlisted applicants for the first cohort of its Regulatory Sandbox
label: Primary

headline: Raqami Islamic Digital Bank Becomes a Scheduled Bank
annotation: Raqami Islamic Digital Bank obtained scheduled bank status, after Mashreq Bank Pakistan in September 2025. Two more digital banks are now operating, which raises competition for digital first retail products.
sourceTitle: Annual Payment Systems Review FY 2025-26, p. 21
label: Primary

headline: Cyber Shield Cyber Resilience Strategy (2025 to 2030)
annotation: CRMD Circular Letter No. 01 of 2026 launched a phased cyber resilience roadmap for SBP regulated entities, covering governance, detection and response, recovery, skills and third party risk. Regulated entities must align their own cybersecurity programmes with it.
sourcePublisher: State Bank of Pakistan (text read via a RegAlert copy)
sourceTitle: CRMD Circular Letter No. 01 of 2026
label: Primary text via a third party copy

headline: Virtual Assets Act 2026 Passed
annotation: Parliament passed the Virtual Assets Act 2026, putting the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA), first set up by a 2025 ordinance, on a statutory footing. It provides for licensing of virtual asset service providers, market surveillance and AML compliance, with coordination with SBP and SECP. Reports I read do not describe a stablecoin framework.
sourceTitle: Pakistan passes Virtual Assets Act 2026, empowers regulator to combat money laundering
label: Secondary (Act text not read)

headline: Banks Allowed to Serve Licensed Virtual Asset Service Providers
annotation: An SBP circular replaced the 2018 ban on dealing in virtual currencies. Banks may open accounts for PVARA licensed providers and their customers, with client money kept in segregated, rupee denominated, non remunerative accounts and no cash in or out. This opens banking rails for licensed crypto businesses under tight controls.
sourceTitle: SBP replaces 2018 crypto ban with new VASP rules
label: Secondary (circular number and exact date not confirmed)

headline: Draft Open Banking Regulations 2026 Released for Consultation
annotation: SBP published draft Open Banking Regulations for public consultation. The draft would require banks, microfinance banks and EMIs to open APIs to licensed third party providers, with Raast as a central API hub and explicit, time bound, revocable customer consent. It builds on the open banking sandbox cohort. For builders, this is the clearest signal yet of how account information and payment initiation services will work.
sourcePublisher: State Bank of Pakistan, Payment Systems Policy and Oversight Department
sourceTitle: Open Banking Regulations 2026, draft for public consultation (pp. 5 to 8; date from PDF metadata and press coverage)
label: Primary
